blocks.text:
Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 13
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/13
- **Title**: gh-12 Add a login page with Google/Apple sign-in and account remember
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-12` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +1872
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T11:24:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T11:42:03Z

## PR Description

Closes #12
### What changed
Added a login page with Google/Apple sign-in and a remembered account: `SessionController` (ChangeNotifier) orchestrates restore/sign-in/sign-out over an injectable `AuthService` (`google_sign_in` 7.x + `sign_in_with_apple`) and `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`). App start auto-restores the remembered account, skipping the login page; sign-out clears it.

### Key decisions
- `AuthService` returns `null` on user cancellation (not an exception) so the UI can distinguish "backed out" from "failed"; non-cancellation errors surface as inline login errors
- Platform convention honored via `defaultTargetPlatform`: Apple button on iOS/macOS only, Google button everywhere
- Apple's nullable profile fields (name/email only arrive on first authorization) modeled in `AppUser` (`toJson`/`fromJson` for persistence, nullable fields by design)
- Google sign-out is best-effort and initializes the SDK first — devices without Google services can still sign out of the local session
- `GoogleSignInPlatform`/`SignInWithApplePlatform` instances faked in tests — no plugin channels touched in the suite

### How to verify
```bash
flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test      # 46 tests: model, store, controller, login/home/app flows
```
Widget tests cover the login page (buttons per platform, remember-me, busy/error states), session restore across simulated restarts, and sign-out returning to login.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  APP[DmToolsApp] -->|restore| SC[SessionController]
  SC -->|signIn google/apple| AUTH[GoogleAppleAuthService]
  SC -->|save/clear/load| STORE[SharedPreferencesSessionStore]
  APP -->|restoring| SPLASH[Splash]
  APP -->|signedOut| LOGIN[LoginPage]
  APP -->|signedIn| HOME[HomePage + Sign out]
  HOME -->|signOut| SC
```

</details>

blocks.text:
Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 13
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/13
- **Title**: gh-12 Add a login page with Google/Apple sign-in and account remember
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-12` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +1872
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T11:24:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T11:42:03Z

## PR Description

Closes #12
### What changed
Added a login page with Google/Apple sign-in and a remembered account: `SessionController` (ChangeNotifier) orchestrates restore/sign-in/sign-out over an injectable `AuthService` (`google_sign_in` 7.x + `sign_in_with_apple`) and `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`). App start auto-restores the remembered account, skipping the login page; sign-out clears it.

### Key decisions
- `AuthService` returns `null` on user cancellation (not an exception) so the UI can distinguish "backed out" from "failed"; non-cancellation errors surface as inline login errors
- Platform convention honored via `defaultTargetPlatform`: Apple button on iOS/macOS only, Google button everywhere
- Apple's nullable profile fields (name/email only arrive on first authorization) modeled in `AppUser` (`toJson`/`fromJson` for persistence, nullable fields by design)
- Google sign-out is best-effort and initializes the SDK first — devices without Google services can still sign out of the local session
- `GoogleSignInPlatform`/`SignInWithApplePlatform` instances faked in tests — no plugin channels touched in the suite

### How to verify
```bash
flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test      # 46 tests: model, store, controller, login/home/app flows
```
Widget tests cover the login page (buttons per platform, remember-me, busy/error states), session restore across simulated restarts, and sign-out returning to login.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  APP[DmToolsApp] -->|restore| SC[SessionController]
  SC -->|signIn google/apple| AUTH[GoogleAppleAuthService]
  SC -->|save/clear/load| STORE[SharedPreferencesSessionStore]
  APP -->|restoring| SPLASH[Splash]
  APP -->|signedOut| LOGIN[LoginPage]
  APP -->|signedIn| HOME[HomePage + Sign out]
  HOME -->|signOut| SC
```

</details>

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# pr-13: gh-12 Add a login page with Google/Apple sign-in and account remember

## Description

Closes #12
### What changed
Added a login page with Google/Apple sign-in and a remembered account: `SessionController` (ChangeNotifier) orchestrates restore/sign-in/sign-out over an injectable `AuthService` (`google_sign_in` 7.x + `sign_in_with_apple`) and `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`). App start auto-restores the remembered account, skipping the login page; sign-out clears it.

### Key decisions
- `AuthService` returns `null` on user cancellation (not an exception) so the UI can distinguish "backed out" from "failed"; non-cancellation errors surface as inline login errors
- Platform convention honored via `defaultTargetPlatform`: Apple button on iOS/macOS only, Google button everywhere
- Apple's nullable profile fields (name/email only arrive on first authorization) modeled in `AppUser` (`toJson`/`fromJson` for persistence, nullable fields by design)
- Google sign-out is best-effort and initializes the SDK first — devices without Google services can still sign out of the local session
- `GoogleSignInPlatform`/`SignInWithApplePlatform` instances faked in tests — no plugin channels touched in the suite

### How to verify
```bash
flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test      # 46 tests: model, store, controller, login/home/app flows
```
Widget tests cover the login page (buttons per platform, remember-me, busy/error states), session restore across simulated restarts, and sign-out returning to login.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  APP[DmToolsApp] -->|restore| SC[SessionController]
  SC -->|signIn google/apple| AUTH[GoogleAppleAuthService]
  SC -->|save/clear/load| STORE[SharedPreferencesSessionStore]
  APP -->|restoring| SPLASH[Splash]
  APP -->|signedOut| LOGIN[LoginPage]
  APP -->|signedIn| HOME[HomePage + Sign out]
  HOME -->|signOut| SC
```

The `addPostFrameCallback` calls `_controller.restore()` without awaiting/catching — an async error. On Windows/Linux, google_sign_in 7.x has no implementation → sign-in would fail with an exception (caught by controller, shown as error). OK.

So `signInWithGoogle()` on an unsupported platform throws MissingPluginException (probably) → controller catches `on Exception` → shows inline error. That works, awkward UX but works.

For signOut(): if `_ensureGoogleInitialized()` throws MissingPluginException (not GoogleSignInException), it escapes `GoogleAppleAuthService.signOut` — un-caught (only GoogleSignInException is caught). Then SessionController.signOut() propagates → in HomePage, `onPressed: () => controller.signOut()` — unawaited future → unhandled async error, and the store never clears, user stays signed in, busy stuck true! Wait — `signOut()` in the controller: `_busy = true; notifyListeners(); await _authService.signOut();` — if that throws, `_busy` stays true and status stays signedIn. No try/finally in signOut()! That's an asymetry bug: `_signIn` has try/finally protecting busy, `signOut()` does not. If auth.signOut() or store.clear() throws, the controller is left busy=true forever → all login buttons permanently disabled (though user is on home page) and the app can't sign out. In the real Google path, GoogleSignInException is swallowed by the service; but store.clear() could throw? SharedPreferences.remove rarely throws. MissingPluginException case above (desktop) is real if the app ever runs on desktop: user signs in with... wait on desktop they can't sign in successfully at all (Google fails, Apple not shown) so they can't reach HomePage. Hmm — unless restored from previous mobile session? Cross-device restore isn't a thing here (local storage only).

OK so realistically signOut() failure modes: (1) `SessionStore.clear()` throwing → busy stuck. (2) non-GoogleSignInException from Google plugin. Both are unlikely but the missing try/finally asymetry is a legitimate IMPORTANT robustness finding (defensive, cheap to fix).

Let me double-check the google_sign_in 7.x behavior for `initialize()` on unsupported platforms. From the google_sign_in 7.x changelog/README: "Calling initialize() is required before authenticate()". The interface has `GoogleSignInPlatform.instance` which on missing platform implementation returns a `DefaultGoogleSignInPlatform` whose methods throw MissingPluginException via method channel. But wait — google_sign_in 7.x introduced `GoogleSignInException` wrapping in the app-facing layer? I recall `GoogleSignIn` wraps errors from the platform into GoogleSignInException... Actually in 7.x, `GoogleSignInException` is thrown by the platform interface implementations themselves (each platform impl maps native errors). The default/stub method-channel impl throws MissingPluginException directly. Hmm, I'm not certain enough. This nuance only matters for desktop; mobile is the target. I'll fold the "catch only GoogleSignInException" observation into the signOut robustness finding as supporting context, phrased carefully.

**`_signIn` while status == signedIn?** Not reachable from UI.

**`busy` guard against double-tap:** buttons disabled while busy — handled via onPressed null. Race: rapid double-tap before notifyListeners renders? First tap sets busy synchronously before awaiting? `_signIn` sets `_busy = true; notifyListeners();` synchronously at the start (before first await)... Actually `signInWithGoogle({required bool remember})` returns `_signIn(...)` — async function body runs synchronously until first await. `_busy = true; notifyListeners();` run sync, then `await flow()`. But UI tap → two taps in same frame? Second tap would call _signIn again before rebuild disables button? In practice taps are separate events with rebuilds between (notifyListeners triggers rebuild next frame). Test-wise fine. Flutter processes tap events then rebuilds before next tap typically (next frame). Not a real issue.

**`restore()` and `addPostFrameCallback` on injected controller in tests:** fine.

**Stale `restore()` in `didChangeDependencies`?** Not needed.

**`AppUser.fromJson` throw inside `load()` → unhandled in `restore()` (covered above).**

**`HomePage._initialFor` returns `''` for Apple without name:** `CircleAvatar` child Text(') — renders empty avatar. Minor cosmetic: for apple fallback the initial is empty string while the display name fallback is 'Apple account'. Inconsistent — the avatar shows nothing while name shows "Apple account". SUGESTION (could use 'A').

Wait actually let me re-check: `_initialFor` returns 'G' for google fallback and `''` for apple. That's clearly a small oversight — 'A' was intended presumably. Minor.

**`LoginPage` error text leaks full exception toString:** SUGESTION/IMPORTANT (UX).

**`_GoogleGlyph`**: cosmetic placeholder "G" text. It's an example app; fine, maybe SUGESTION to use a real asset/icon. Not worth much.

**`appleSignInAvailable` computed at build each time via defaultTargetPlatform — fine. But tests override with debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride; several tests set it and reset to null at the end — if an expectation throws before reset, the override leaks to other tests. Best practice is addTearDown. Minor test hygiene: SUGESTION. Actually wait — this IS a real test-robustness issue: `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride = null` at the end of test body; if an expect fails, override leaks into subsequent tests (they set their own at start though — every test in login_page_test sets it at start). Every test sets it, so leak is bounded. SUGESTION.

### 3. Architecture / OP

- Clean layering: domain / services / ui. DI via constructor injection. Good.
- `GoogleAppleAuthService` handles both providers — named OK.
- `SessionController` extends ChangeNotifier — fine.
- `InMemorySessionStore` in lib/ — "for tests and previews" — shipping test-only class in production code (lib/). Minor: could live in test helpers; but it's a common pattern to keep in lib for dev previews. SUGESTION.
- `_RecordingStore` duplicated across three test files (session_controller_test, home_page_test, login_page_test) and `SharedMemorySessionStore` in widget_test — duplication! Four in-memory store implementations across test files while `InMemorySessionStore` already exists in lib. That's a legit duplication finding (IMPORTANT per guidelines "Duplication" dimension — duplicated logic across files). Actually the _RecordingStore variants record call counts, InMemorySessionStore doesn't. Still, they're near-identical to each other — could share one fake in test/fakes/. SUGESTION-to-IMPORTANT. I'd say SUGESTION since tests are clear and small; but guidelines explicitly list duplication as a dimension. I'll make it a SUGESTION with a note.

### 4. Tests

- Good coverage: model, store, auth service, controller, pages, app flows. 46 tests claimed.
- `expect(store.load(), completion(isNotNull))` — works, though awaiting would be cleaner.
- Missing test: `restore()` with corrupted JSON (would document the crash path).
- Missing test: controller.signOut() when auth.signOut throws (busy stuck bug undocumented).

### 5. pubspec

- `google_sign_in: ^7.2.0`, `sign_in_with_apple: ^8.2.0`, `shared_preferences: ^2.5.6` — reasonable.
- dev_dependencies add platform interfaces for fakes — good practice.
- No new heavy deps. Fine.

### 6. Platform config

Ticket: "Add a login page with Google/Apple sign-in". Real Google sign-in on iOS/Android requires native configuration (Info.plist URL schemes, GoogleService-Info.plist / meta-data in AndroidManifest, CFBundleVersion etc.; Apple sign-in requires entitlement + capability). The PR touches only Dart + pubspec — no android/ or ios/ changes! Let me verify: diff shows no android/ios changes. So on a real device:

Actually google_sign_in 7.x on Android works with just the dependency if the OAuth client is configured via google-services.json or `com.google.android.gms...` meta-data? In 7.x, authenticate() on Android uses Credential Manager; it requires configuring `OAuth Web Client ID` via `initialize(clientId: ...)` or an embedded meta-data tag. The verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings: broken behavior... The code compiles and tests pass; on-device it will throw at runtime without config. I'll rate IMPORTANT (deployment/config gap), phrased as a question about scope.

Let me verify whether android/ios folders contain any Google/Apple config that already exists. Let me grep.

The controller handles errors internally (catches Exception) — but if flow() itself throws synchronously... it's async, returns future; errors caught inside _signIn's try/catch... wait `_signIn` catches `on Exception`. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

## Analysis

### 1. Security issues

**Session restore without re-authentication (potential security concern):** `restore()` just loads the persisted account from `shared_preferences` and sets status to signedIn. This is the "remember me" pattern — typical for consumer apps, not a security issue per se. However, an important detail: the account is trusted locally. Not a blocker for an example app.

**`jsonDecode(raw) as Map<String, dynamic>` unguarded in `load()`**: If the stored value is corrupted (not valid JSON, or JSON but not a Map, or `provider` unknown, or `id` missing), `AppUser.fromJson` throws (ArgumentError or TypeError). `restore()` does NOT wrap `_sessionStore.load()` in try/catch — an unhandled exception in `restore()` would leave the controller stuck in `SessionStatus.restoring` forever (the splash screen forever), because the exception propagates out of `restore()` before `notifyListeners()`. The `addPostFrameCallback` calls `_controller.restore()` without awaiting/catching — an async error. In production, a corrupted prefs entry (e.g., from schema evolution or a manual change) bricks the app on the splash screen. This is a real correctness/robustness issue: **BLOCKING or IMPORTANT?** It's a crash/freeze path triggered by corrupted storage. The restore path catches nothing. Since the app is stuck on splash forever (unrecoverable without reinstall/clear-data), I'd rate it IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING. It's a genuine bug: error path not handled. The guidelines say "Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed?" — here failures aren't swallowed, they crash the restore. Since CI is green and the app works in the happy path, this is a "real maintainability or correctness issue" — IMPORTANT at minimum. Actually, let me think about severity: "BLOCKING — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break." A corrupted storage entry → app stuck on splash forever → that's a bug that would occur in production. But it requires a corrupted prefs entry to trigger, which can happen through app upgrades/version migrations. Given the review verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings: broken behavior. Hmm. The restore() call has `if (_status != SessionStatus.restoring) return;` — restore is called once. If load() throws, status stays restoring → splash forever. I'll classify as IMPORTANT (edge case requiring corrupted storage), but honestly it's a genuine correctness issue worth fixing. Let me think about what triggers corruption realistically: `shared_preferences` values are written by the app itself. AppUser.toJson always produces a Map with valid provider names. The realistic trigger is an app version change where the enum name changed (not here) or a user rooting the device. It's a robustness issue — IMPORTANT.

Wait — but actually there's a subtle real-world trigger: `AppUser.fromJson` casts `json['id'] as String`. jsonDecode of the stored string always gives String for id since we wrote it. OK, realistically rare. IMPORTANT.

**`_signIn` catches only `Exception`, not `Error`:** `on Exception catch` — if the auth service throws an `Error` (e.g., TypeError from a platform interface mismatch), it propagates. Minor; standard Dart practice catches Exception. Not a finding worth much.

**Busy-state reset on error in `_signIn`:** finally sets `_busy = false` and notifies. Good.

**Cancellation during a sign-in while `_status == signedIn`?** Can't happen from UI (login page only shows when signedOut). OK.

**Error message raw `exception.toString()` displayed in UI:** `'Sign-in failed: ${controller.error}'` — shows raw exception text (which may contain internal details) to the user. Minor UX/security hygiene: SUGESTION.

**`credential.identityToken` used as `id` fallback:** The identityToken is a JWT — using it as a stable account identifier is questionable (it changes per authorization — JWTs contain iat/exp so they differ each time!). Apple's identityToken is a fresh JWT per sign-in, so using it as a stable "id" breaks the "stable identifier" contract: each sign-in would produce a different AppUser id → remembered accounts would mismatch on restore... well, restore just loads what was persisted, so it still "works", but two sign-ins from the same Apple account produce different ids. In practice `userIdentifier` is always present on iOS, and sign_in_with_apple on Android/web may return null userIdentifier. This is a design smell; but the comment acknowledges the fallback. It also stores the identityToken (a credential-ish bearer token) into shared_preferences plaintext via toJson — wait, no: the identityToken is only used as `id` in the fallback case, and then it IS persisted to shared_preferences as part of AppUser.toJson. Storing an OAuth identity token (JWT) in plaintext local storage is a mild security concern — tokens should not be persisted; user identifiers should. But it only happens in the fallback path where userIdentifier is null. Hmm, on iOS userIdentifier is non-null. On Android (sign_in_with_apple supports Android via web), userIdentifier is null and identityToken is the JWT. So on Android the JWT gets persisted. That's worth flaging as IMPORTANT security hygiene... Let me be careful: is persisting an Apple identityToken a security issue? An identityToken is a short-lived JWT (audience = app's Services ID). Persisted plaintext in app-private storage. The app's storage is sandboxed (shared_preferences → app-private). Risk is low; it's not a "secret" per se, but it is a token. I'd raise SUGESTION/IMPORTANT: prefer deriving a stable local id (e.g., hash of the token's `sub` claim) rather than persisting the raw token. Since the token contains `sub` (the stable Apple user id), parsing the JWT's sub claim would give the true stable identifier. That's a legit suggestion with real merit.

Also `id: ... ?? 'apple-unknown'` — if both null, ALL such users share id 'apple-unknown'. With single-account store, signing in two different Apple accounts both with null identifiers would be conflated. Edge case; SUGESTION.

**`restore()` no-op guard vs post-frame callback:** In `DmToolsApp.initState`, restore is called via addPostFrameCallback. In widget tests, pumpAndSetle handles it. Fine.

**`_google` getter + `_googleInitialized` flag with injected override:** Tests inject platform instances (GoogleSignInPlatform.instance = fake), and `GoogleSignIn.instance` is a singleton that delegates to the platform interface. The service caches `_googleInitialized` but if `GoogleAppleAuthService` were created twice, each has its own flag — fine. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 13
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/13
- **Title**: gh-12 Add a login page with Google/Apple sign-in and account remember
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-12` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +1872
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T11:24:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T11:42:03Z

## PR Description

Closes #12
### What changed
Added a login page with Google/Apple sign-in and a remembered account: `SessionController` (ChangeNotifier) orchestrates restore/sign-in/sign-out over an injectable `AuthService` (`google_sign_in` 7.x + `sign_in_with_apple`) and `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`). App start auto-restores the remembered account, skipping the login page; sign-out clears it.

### Key decisions
- `AuthService` returns `null` on user cancellation (not an exception) so the UI can distinguish "backed out" from "failed"; non-cancellation errors surface as inline login errors
- Platform convention honored via `defaultTargetPlatform`: Apple button on iOS/macOS only, Google button everywhere
- Apple's nullable profile fields (name/email only arrive on first authorization) modeled in `AppUser` (`toJson`/`fromJson` for persistence, nullable fields by design)
- Google sign-out is best-effort and initializes the SDK first — devices without Google services can still sign out of the local session
- `GoogleSignInPlatform`/`SignInWithApplePlatform` instances faked in tests — no plugin channels touched in the suite

### How to verify
```bash
flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test      # 46 tests: model, store, controller, login/home/app flows
```
Widget tests cover the login page (buttons per platform, remember-me, busy/error states), session restore across simulated restarts, and sign-out returning to login.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  APP[DmToolsApp] -->|restore| SC[SessionController]
  SC -->|signIn google/apple| AUTH[GoogleAppleAuthService]
  SC -->|save/clear/load| STORE[SharedPreferencesSessionStore]
  APP -->|restoring| SPLASH[Splash]
  APP -->|signedOut| LOGIN[LoginPage]
  APP -->|signedIn| HOME[HomePage + Sign out]
  HOME -->|signOut| SC
```

</details>

**Session restore without re-authentication (potential security concern):** `restore()` just loads the persisted account from `shared_preferences` and sets status to signedIn. This is the "remember me" pattern — typical for consumer apps, not a security issue per se. However, an important detail: the account is trusted locally. Not a blocker for an example app.

This is a real correctness/robustness issue: **BLOCKING or IMPORTANT?** It's a crash/freeze path triggered by corrupted storage. The restore path catches nothing. Since the app is stuck on splash forever (unrecoverable without reinstall/clear-data), I'd rate it IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING. It's a genuine bug: error path not handled. The guidelines say "Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed?" — here failures aren't swallowed, they crash the restore. A corrupted storage entry → app stuck on splash forever → that's a bug that would occur in production. But it requires a corrupted prefs entry to trigger, which can happen through app upgrades/version migrations. Given the review verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings: broken behavior. Let me think about what triggers corruption realistically: `shared_preferences` values are written by the app itself. AppUser.toJson always produces a Map with valid provider names. The realistic trigger is an app version change where the enum name changed (not here) or a user rooting the device. It's a robustness issue — IMPORTANT.

Wait — but actually there's a subtle real-world trigger: `AppUser.fromJson` casts `json['id'] as String`. jsonDecode of the stored string always gives String for id since we wrote it. OK, realistically rare. IMPORTANT.

**`_signIn` catches only `Exception`, not `Error`:** `on Exception catch` — if the auth service throws an `Error` (e.g., TypeError from a platform interface mismatch), it propagates. Minor; standard Dart practice catches Exception. Not a finding worth much.

On Android (sign_in_with_apple supports Android via web), userIdentifier is null and identityToken is the JWT. So on Android the JWT gets persisted. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 13
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/13
- **Title**: gh-12 Add a login page with Google/Apple sign-in and account remember
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-12` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +1872
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T11:24:52Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-21T11:42:03Z

## PR Description

Closes #12
### What changed
Added a login page with Google/Apple sign-in and a remembered account: `SessionController` (ChangeNotifier) orchestrates restore/sign-in/sign-out over an injectable `AuthService` (`google_sign_in` 7.x + `sign_in_with_apple`) and `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`). App start auto-restores the remembered account, skipping the login page; sign-out clears it.

### Key decisions
- `AuthService` returns `null` on user cancellation (not an exception) so the UI can distinguish "backed out" from "failed"; non-cancellation errors surface as inline login errors
- Platform convention honored via `defaultTargetPlatform`: Apple button on iOS/macOS only, Google button everywhere
- Apple's nullable profile fields (name/email only arrive on first authorization) modeled in `AppUser` (`toJson`/`fromJson` for persistence, nullable fields by design)
- Google sign-out is best-effort and initializes the SDK first — devices without Google services can still sign out of the local session
- `GoogleSignInPlatform`/`SignInWithApplePlatform` instances faked in tests — no plugin channels touched in the suite

### How to verify
```bash
flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test      # 46 tests: model, store, controller, login/home/app flows
```
Widget tests cover the login page (buttons per platform, remember-me, busy/error states), session restore across simulated restarts, and sign-out returning to login.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  APP[DmToolsApp] -->|restore| SC[SessionController]
  SC -->|signIn google/apple| AUTH[GoogleAppleAuthService]
  SC -->|save/clear/load| STORE[SharedPreferencesSessionStore]
  APP -->|restoring| SPLASH[Splash]
  APP -->|signedOut| LOGIN[LoginPage]
  APP -->|signedIn| HOME[HomePage + Sign out]
  HOME -->|signOut| SC
```

</details>
